title: Exam Cram
subject: respiratory
introMarkdown: **Quick Scan:** Short, bolded terms, definitions, pathways, comparisons, and high-yield associations. For fuller explanations switch to **Detailed Review**.
subtitle: Quick Scan

sections.title: Seven Functions and Upper/Lower Divisions
sections.markdown:
- **Gas exchange:** O₂ enters blood; CO₂ leaves it.
- **Air movement:** Ventilates the lungs.
- **Environmental protection:** Conditions inspired air; limits drying and temperature changes.
- **Defense:** Filters/traps particles and pathogens.
- **Sound production:** Supports voice.
- **Olfaction:** Carries odorants to smell receptors.
- **Acid–base regulation:** Ventilation changes CO₂ and blood pH.

**Upper tract:** Nose, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, pharynx — **warm, humidify, filter**.

**Lower tract:** Larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, lungs.

- **Conducting zone:** Nose → **terminal bronchioles**; carries/conditions air.
- **Respiratory zone:** **Respiratory bronchioles** → alveolar ducts/sacs → alveoli; gas exchange.

sections.title: Nose, Pharynx, and Airflow Route
sections.markdown:
**Air route:** Nostrils → nasal cavity → **choanae** → nasopharynx → oropharynx → laryngopharynx → larynx → trachea → **primary → secondary → tertiary bronchi** → bronchioles → terminal bronchioles → respiratory bronchioles → alveolar ducts → alveoli.

- **Alae:** Lateral walls of nostrils.
- **Nasal vestibule:** Space just inside nostrils.
- **Vibrissae:** Nasal hairs trapping coarse particles.
- **Superior/middle/inferior conchae:** Increase air–mucosa contact.
- **Meatuses:** Passages beneath corresponding conchae.
- **Hard palate:** Bony anterior separation of mouth and nasal cavity.
- **Soft palate:** Muscular posterior palate; **uvula:** Hanging projection.
- **Nasopharynx:** Upper pharynx; auditory-tube openings and pharyngeal tonsil.
- **Oropharynx:** Behind mouth.
- **Laryngopharynx:** Shared inferior passage toward airway/esophagus.

**Nasal breathing:** Warming + humidification + filtration + olfaction; nasal nitric oxide is present. Do not assume it always raises oxygen saturation.

sections.title: Respiratory Mucosa, Lamina Propria, and Mucus Escalator
sections.markdown:
- **Respiratory epithelium:** Mostly **pseudostratified ciliated columnar** with mucus-producing cells in large conducting airways.
- **Lamina propria:** Connective tissue beneath epithelium; vessels, glands, immune support.
- **Respiratory mucosa:** Epithelium + supporting lamina propria.
- **Mucociliary/mucus escalator:** **Mucus traps** debris → **cilia move** mucus toward pharynx → swallow or cough out.
- **Alveolar macrophages:** Remove particles that reach gas-exchange regions.

**Recall:** **Mucus catches; cilia carry.**

sections.title: Regional Histology Identification
sections.markdown:
- **Nasal respiratory region / nasopharynx:** Mainly pseudostratified **ciliated columnar**.
- **Oropharynx / laryngopharynx:** **Nonkeratinized stratified squamous**; resists food abrasion.
- **Trachea / larger bronchi:** Pseudostratified ciliated columnar; mucus production.
- **Bronchioles:** Progress toward **simple columnar/cuboidal**; fewer cilia; club cells.
- **Alveoli:** **Simple squamous**, mostly **type I pneumocytes**; shortest gas-diffusion path.

**Pattern:** Larger airways = **protection and clearance**; alveoli = **thin exchange surface**. Nasal olfactory/vestibular regions are exceptions to the usual respiratory lining.

sections.title: Laryngeal Cartilages, Folds, and Voice
sections.markdown:
- **Larynx:** Open airway + protection during swallowing + voice production.
- **Unpaired cartilages (3):** **Epiglottic, thyroid, cricoid**.
- **Paired cartilage types (3):** **Arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform**.
- **Thyroid cartilage:** Laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
- **Cricoid:** Complete cartilage ring inferior to thyroid cartilage.
- **Arytenoids:** Move true vocal folds; help open/close glottis.
- **Vestibular folds:** **False vocal cords**; protective.
- **Vocal folds:** **True vocal cords**; vibrate to produce voice.
- **Glottis:** Opening between the true vocal folds.
- **Phonation:** Producing voiced sound.
- **Articulation:** Shaping sound into speech (tongue, lips, palate, etc.).
- **Pitch:** Changes with vocal-fold **tension, length, and mass/thickness**; more tension usually raises pitch.
- **Intrinsic muscles:** Move/tension folds; regulate glottic opening.
- **Extrinsic muscles:** Raise/lower and position the whole larynx.
- **Epiglottis:** Helps divert swallowed material away from airway; not the only protective mechanism.

sections.title: Epiglottis and Cough Reflex Sequence
sections.markdown:
**Cough sequence:** Irritant stimulates airway receptors → sensory signal to **medulla** → glottis closes → expiratory muscles raise thoracic pressure → glottis opens → explosive airflow expels material.

- **Epiglottis:** Helps protect airway during swallowing.
- **Glottis:** Opening between true vocal folds.
- **Cough:** Reflex clearance using pressure and rapid expiration.

**Exam contrast:** Epiglottis ≠ glottis.

sections.title: Trachea, Carina, Bronchi and Autonomic Effects
sections.markdown:
- **Trachea:** About **15–20 C-shaped cartilage supports**; posterior opening leaves room for esophagus.
- **Trachealis:** Posterior smooth muscle; adjusts tracheal diameter.
- **Elastic ligaments/tissue:** Permit stretch and recoil.
- **Carina:** Ridge at division into right/left main bronchi.
- **Primary (main) bronchi:** Enter each lung.
- **Secondary (lobar) bronchi:** One per lobe: **right 3, left 2**.
- **Tertiary (segmental) bronchi:** Supply bronchopulmonary segments.
- **Bronchioles:** **No cartilage**; significant smooth-muscle control.
- **Right main bronchus:** Usually wider, shorter, more vertical; aspiration more likely.
- **Sympathetic/β₂:** Generally **bronchodilation**.
- **Parasympathetic/cholinergic:** Generally **bronchoconstriction**.

**Route:** Main → lobar → segmental → smaller bronchi → bronchioles → terminal → respiratory bronchioles → alveolar ducts → alveoli.

**Lecture association:** Trachealis tends toward relaxation with sympathetic influence; contraction with parasympathetic influence.

sections.title: Lung Lobes, Fissures, and Pleura
sections.markdown:
- **Right lung:** **3 lobes** — superior, middle, inferior; **horizontal + oblique fissures**.
- **Left lung:** **2 lobes** — superior, inferior; **oblique fissure**; **cardiac notch**.
- **Apex:** Superior tip; **base:** Inferior diaphragmatic surface.
- **Costal surface:** Faces ribs; **mediastinal surface:** Faces middle of thorax.
- **Hilum:** Entry/exit of bronchi, pulmonary vessels, nerves, lymphatics.
- **Visceral pleura:** Adheres to lung surface.
- **Parietal pleura:** Lines chest wall.
- **Pleural cavity:** Thin, fluid-containing **potential space** between layers; limits friction and assists lung expansion with thorax.

**Know on model:** Lung sides/lobes/fissures; cardiac notch; apex/base; hilar region; visceral/parietal pleura; diaphragm.

sections.title: Alveolar Cell Types and Respiratory Membrane
sections.markdown:
- **Type I pneumocytes:** Thin **simple squamous** gas-exchange cells; most alveolar surface.
- **Type II pneumocytes:** Produce **surfactant**; reduces surface tension and alveolar collapse.
- **Alveolar macrophages (dust cells):** Phagocytose debris/microbes.
- **Alveolar ducts:** Lead to alveolar sacs and alveoli.
- **Pulmonary capillaries:** Surround alveoli for exchange.
- **Respiratory membrane:** **Type I alveolar epithelium + (often fused) basement membranes + capillary endothelium**.

**Direction:** **O₂ alveolus → blood; CO₂ blood → alveolus.**

**Why thin?** Short diffusion distance increases gas-exchange efficiency.

sections.title: External, Internal, and Cellular Respiration
sections.markdown:
**Instructor's three steps of external respiration:**
1. **Pulmonary ventilation:** Air enters/leaves alveoli.
2. **Pulmonary gas exchange:** O₂ into blood; CO₂ into alveoli.
3. **Blood transport:** Circulation carries gases between lungs and tissues.

- **Internal respiration:** O₂ moves **blood → tissues**; CO₂ moves **tissues → blood**.
- **Cellular respiration:** Cells use fuel and, in aerobic metabolism, O₂ to produce ATP.

**Terminology note:** Some texts use “external respiration” more narrowly for exchange at the lungs; know the instructor's **three-step list**.

sections.title: Boyle’s Law and Pressure Direction
sections.markdown:
- **Boyle's law:** Pressure inversely related to volume at constant temperature and gas amount.
- **Equation:** **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**.
- **Inspiration:** Thoracic/lung **volume ↑ → alveolar pressure ↓** below atmosphere → air **in**.
- **Expiration:** Lung **volume ↓ → alveolar pressure ↑** above atmosphere → air **out**.
- **Atmospheric pressure (sea-level example):** ~**760 mmHg**.
- **Inspiring alveoli (lecture example):** ~**759 mmHg**; **expiring:** ~**761 mmHg**.
- **Intrapulmonary pressure:** Pressure within alveoli.
- **Intrapleural pressure:** Pressure in pleural space; not the same as alveolar pressure.

**Fast recall:** **Volume up → pressure down → air in.**

sections.title: Inspiration, Expiration, Primary Muscles
sections.markdown:
- **Quiet breathing (eupnea):** Inspiration **active**; expiration usually **passive**.
- **Primary inspiratory muscles (2):** **Diaphragm + external intercostals**.
- **Inspiration:** Diaphragm **contracts/descends**; ribs elevate; volume ↑; pressure ↓.
- **Quiet expiration:** Diaphragm **relaxes/ascends**; elastic recoil; volume ↓; pressure ↑.
- **Forced inspiration:** Adds accessory muscles (e.g., **scalenes, sternocleidomastoid**).
- **Forced expiration:** **Abdominals + internal intercostals** actively help expel air.
- **Forced breathing:** Greater muscular effort than quiet breathing.

**Exam distinction:** Quiet expiration does **not** normally require active abdominal contraction.

sections.title: Four Volumes, Vital Capacity, and Total Lung Capacity
sections.markdown:
**Four respiratory volumes:**
- **TV (tidal volume):** Ordinary quiet breath; ~**500 mL** in standard classroom example.
- **IRV:** Extra inhaled after normal inspiration.
- **ERV:** Extra exhaled after normal expiration.
- **RV:** Air remaining after maximal expiration.

**Capacities:**
- **IC = TV + IRV**.
- **FRC = ERV + RV**.
- **VC (vital capacity) = IRV + TV + ERV**.
- **TLC (total lung capacity) = VC + RV**.

**Exam trap:** **VC excludes RV; TLC includes RV.** Simple spirometry does not directly measure RV.

sections.title: Henry’s Law, Gas Gradients, and Exchange
sections.markdown:
- **Partial pressure (Pₒ₂, P꜀ₒ₂):** Pressure contribution of an individual gas.
- **Henry's law:** Dissolved gas concentration depends on its **partial pressure and solubility** at a given temperature.
- **Diffusion:** Each gas moves down its **own partial-pressure gradient**.

**At lungs:** **O₂ alveoli → blood**; **CO₂ blood → alveoli**.

**At tissues:** **O₂ blood → cells**; **CO₂ cells → blood**.

- **Why exchange works:** Thin respiratory membrane; maintained partial-pressure differences.
- **CO₂:** More soluble than O₂; diffuses effectively even across a smaller pressure gradient.

**Contrast:** **Boyle = ventilation pressure/volume. Henry = gas dissolving in liquid.**

sections.title: Oxyhemoglobin, Carbaminohemoglobin, and Saturation
sections.markdown:
- **Hemoglobin (Hb):** Main O₂ carrier inside RBCs.
- **Oxyhemoglobin (HbO₂):** Hb carrying **O₂** at heme iron.
- **Carbaminohemoglobin (HbCO₂):** Hb carrying **CO₂** on globin groups.
- **High Pₒ₂ (lungs):** **O₂ loading**.
- **Low Pₒ₂ (tissues):** **O₂ unloading**.
- **O₂–Hb curve:** **Sigmoidal (S-shaped)** from cooperative binding.
- **Plateau (high Pₒ₂):** High saturation in lungs.
- **Steep region (lower Pₒ₂):** Facilitates unloading in tissues.
- **Right shift:** **CO₂ ↑, H⁺ ↑ (pH ↓), temperature ↑** → lower Hb–O₂ affinity → more release.
- **Left shift:** Greater affinity; less release at same Pₒ₂.
- **Bohr effect:** More CO₂/H⁺ encourages O₂ unloading.

**Recall:** Oxygenated blood is bright red; deoxygenated blood dark red, **not blue**.

sections.title: Three CO2 Routes, Carbonic Anhydrase, and pH
sections.markdown:
**Three CO₂ transport forms (lecture approximations):**
- **~70%:** **Bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻)** pathway.
- **~23%:** **Carbamino compounds**, including Hb–CO₂.
- **~7%:** Physically dissolved CO₂.

- **Carbonic anhydrase:** Enzyme accelerating CO₂ hydration in RBCs.
- **Reaction:** **CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻**.
- **Chloride shift:** RBC exports HCO₃⁻ in exchange for Cl⁻ in systemic capillaries; reverse near lungs.
- **CO₂ retention:** **H⁺ ↑ → pH ↓**; may cause respiratory acidosis.
- **CO₂ exhalation ↑:** **H⁺ ↓ → pH ↑**; may cause respiratory alkalosis.

**Clarification:** The slide calls the ~70% route “carbonic acid,” but **bicarbonate is the principal transported form**; H₂CO₃ is transient.

sections.title: Medullary DRG/VRG and Pontine Centers
sections.markdown:
- **Respiratory rhythmicity centers:** Neural networks primarily in **medulla oblongata**; pons modifies breathing pattern.
- **DRG (dorsal respiratory group):** Basic inspiratory activity/sensory integration; lecture associates with **diaphragm + external intercostals**.
- **VRG (ventral respiratory group):** Stronger/forced respiratory output; lecture emphasizes **accessory muscles**.
- **Apneustic center (pons; older term):** **Promotes inspiration**; lecture says **stimulates DRG**.
- **Pneumotaxic center (pons; older term):** **Limits inspiration**; restrains apneustic influence.
- **Central chemoreception:** Strongly sensitive to **CO₂-related pH changes** in brain/CSF.
- **Peripheral chemoreceptors:** **Carotid/aortic bodies** respond to O₂, CO₂ and pH changes.

**Exam pairing:** **DRG = basic inspiration; VRG = forced patterns; apneustic = stimulate; pneumotaxic = limit.** The discrete-center names are simplified lecture terminology.

sections.title: Named Conditions and Rapid Anatomy Recall
sections.markdown:
**Instructor-named conditions:**
- **Hypoxia:** Insufficient tissue oxygen.
- **Anoxia:** Essentially no available tissue oxygen (slide may say **apoxia**).
- **Laryngitis:** Inflamed larynx; hoarseness.
- **Epiglottitis:** Inflamed/swollen epiglottic region; potential airway emergency.
- **Pneumonia:** Inflamed/infected lung parenchyma; impaired gas exchange.
- **Cystic fibrosis:** Abnormal epithelial ion transport → thick airway mucus.
- **Asthma:** Variable, often reversible airway narrowing with inflammation/hyperresponsiveness.

**Identify on models:** Nasal conchae/meatuses; hard/soft palate; uvula; pharynx subdivisions; epiglottis; thyroid/cricoid/arytenoid/corniculate/cuneiform cartilages; true/false vocal folds; tracheal rings, trachealis, carina; primary/secondary/tertiary bronchi; lung lobes/fissures, cardiac notch, apex/base, pleura, diaphragm; alveolar ducts/alveoli.

**Rapid pairs:** **Type I = diffusion; II = surfactant; macrophage = defense.** **Sympathetic = dilate; parasympathetic = constrict.** **Boyle = inverse P/V; Henry = dissolved gas.** **DRG = quiet inspiration; VRG = stronger/forced effort.** **Most CO₂ = HCO₃⁻.**
